Sign text: The Mansfield Maritime Hammock
This maritime hammock is dedicated in grateful appreciation to Phyllis and Howard Mansfield, residents of Cocoa Beach for over 50 years. It's Brevard County's way of recognizing the Mansfields for their many decades of tireless volunteer work and dedication in protecting this habitat for birds that migrated through Brevard County and nested here; for publishing their observations; and for conducting educational tours through the hammock for the enjoyment of our visitors.

Flooded shoreline habitat containing shallow standing water, emergent vegetation, and trees. Wet soil conditions indicate recent rainfall. Represents a transition between upland vegetation and aquatic habitat.
Lake edge with trail, surrounding trees, and temporary flooding across portions of the path. Mixed vegetation with open water immediately adjacent to the observation point.
Lakeside trail with dense grasses, shrubs, trees, and standing water. Muddy conditions from recent rain. Strong transition between terrestrial vegetation and open water.
Forest trail with dense canopy and abundant leaf litter. Small puddles from recent rainfall along the trail. Mixed trees and understory shrubs dominate the landscape.
Open park area adjacent to a pavilion and lake. Mixture of maintained grass, scattered trees and nearby wetland vegetation. Heavy rain occured during data collection, reducing some visibility.
Pond shoreline with Australian pine trees and sandy soil. Mixed aquatic and terrestrial vegetation present. Standing water visible with dense tree canopy surrounding the shoreline.
Northern Lakeshore location containing forest, trail, shoreline vegetation. Sandy soil with pine needles and leaf litter. Represents mixed woodland adjacent to open water.
Forested trail near the lakeshore with dense canopy. sandy soil, and surrounding shrubs. Limited human infrastructure visible besides trail access. Good representation of wooded park habitat.
Southern portion of Markham Park. Initial reference site documenting vegetation structure and surrounding land cover. Ground photos collected in all six directions.

This is a natural stream that runs into the gulf of Mexico. It flows under a highway and has businesses on the back side of it. Water levels rise from storms but it does not flood. The water is a muddy brown color. The ground is dry and sandy. This water is not used by humans, it protected due to the fact that an endangered plant species lives here. it's a home for many animals and insects. #alwayswater

This is a freshwater lake. It's used for fishing by humans and a home for fish and insects. It's located on the side of a road. It has a dam like drain that it flows into to go under the road to the other side. This prevents flooding. The ground is dry and there is a lot of wildlife in the water. The water has lillypads floating at the surface. Tons of misquitos and I saw a frog. #alwayswater

This is a natural swamp surrounded by houses. People go fishing in this water. This area encounters flooding. This is brackish water that flows into the golf of Mexico. The ground is hard and dry and there are lots of leaves on the ground. I saw 2 lizards run into the water. The water has lillypads and mossy floating at the surface #alwayswater
